enrichment.headline: Accepts a $5.0M CAL FIRE grant to build living schoolyards at Manzanita and MLK Jr. Elementary

enrichment.summary: The district is accepting a state grant to turn the yards at Manzanita Elementary and Martin Luther King Jr. Elementary into "living schoolyards." vendor.name: Northeastern University - Mills College Campus, Lead by Learning

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Northeastern University - Mills College Campus, Lead by Learning - United for Success Academy

enrichment.headline: Accepts Construction Trades Workforce Initiative's no-cost workshops on building trades careers
enrichment.summary: Construction Trades Workforce Initiative of Oakland will develop and run workshops at no cost to the district. The workshops, held at Castlemont High School, aim to raise awareness of and interest in the Building & Construction Trades program among leaders, staff, students and families. The term runs from September 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024 and began before this vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement-2023-2024 - No-Cost - Construction Trades Workforce Initiative - Linked Learning Department

enrichment.headline: Pays a consultant up to $12,000 to train about 250 staff on school threat assessment
enrichment.summary: An independent consultant in Elk Grove will give three trainings to an estimated 250 district staff and partners, including administrators and mental health clinicians. They will learn the University of Virginia's Comprehensive School Threat Assessment Guidelines, which help school teams decide whether a threat is serious and what protective steps to take. The term runs from January 1, 2024 to June 30, 2024 and began before this vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Byron Wong - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Pays Hope Reimagined up to $18,000 for clinical supervision and mental health training at Korematsu Academy
enrichment.summary: Hope Reimagined of Oakland will provide two hours a week of clinical supervision and staff training at Fred T. Korematsu Discovery Academy. The training uses the Neurosequential Model, a framework for understanding how children's brains develop, and supports students with complex mental health needs. The term runs from August 7, 2023 to May 30, 2024 and began before this vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Hope Reimagined - Fred T. Korematsu Discovery Academy

enrichment.headline: Pays East Bay Football Officials Association up to $40,160 for middle and high school football referees
enrichment.summary: The East Bay Football Officials Association of Oakland will provide officials for all middle and high school football and flag football games in the Oakland Athletic League. It will also continue an evaluation program and certification criteria for officials. The term runs from December 11, 2023 to June 30, 2024 and began before this vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - East Bay Football Officials Association (EBFOA) - Oakland Athletic League (OAL)

enrichment.headline: Accepts Fred Finch Youth Center's no-cost therapy sessions for students at Garfield Elementary
enrichment.summary: Fred Finch Youth Center (doing business as Fred Finch Youth & Family Services) of Oakland will provide two therapists at Garfield Elementary School at no cost to the district. They will conduct 45 one-on-one sessions with up to ten students who have mental health needs. The term runs from October 24, 2023 to May 31, 2024 and began before this vote.

vendor.name: Fred Finch Youth Center dba Fred Finch Youth & Family Services

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement-2023-2024 - No-Cost - Fred Finch Youth Center dba Fred Finch Youth & Family Services - Garfield Elementary School

enrichment.headline: Accepts UC's no-cost college advising program at six high schools through June 2026
enrichment.summary: The Regents of the University of California, on behalf of its Destination College Advising Corps, will place College Adviser Fellows at six high schools at no cost to the district. They will provide college awareness, mentoring, preparation and advising to raise the college-going rate. The schools are Castlemont, Fremont, McClymonds, Oakland High, Oakland Technical and Skyline. The term runs from August 1, 2023 to June 30, 2026 and began before this vote.

vendor.name: The Regents of the University of California (Destination College Advising Corps)

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Agreement - The Regents of the University of California - Destination College Advising Corps (DCAC) - FY2023-2024 - Named District Schools

enrichment.headline: Pays UC's Destination College Advising Corps up to $36,000 for college advisers at two high schools
enrichment.summary: The Regents of the University of California, on behalf of its Destination College Advising Corps, will place College Adviser Fellows at Castlemont High School and Oakland High School. They will provide college awareness, mentoring, preparation and advising. The limit is $18,000 per school, up to $36,000 in total. The term runs from August 1, 2023 to June 30, 2024 and began before this vote.

vendor.name: The Regents of the University of California (Destination College Advising Corps)

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Agreement - The Regents of the University of California - Destination College Advising Corps (DCAC) - FY2023-2026 - HS Linked Learning Office

enrichment.headline: Pays America SCORES Bay Area up to $374,172.40 for Saturday sports and after-school programs
enrichment.summary: America SCORES Bay Area of San Francisco will run ten 9-hour Saturday sports sessions this spring and support after-school programs at 28 school sites. It will also take part in National Girls and Women in Sports Day in 2024, focused on upper elementary and middle school girls. The term runs from January 11, 2024 to May 25, 2024.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - America SCORES Bay Area - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Pays Soccer Without Borders up to $63,500 for a 10-week Saturday sports program for newcomer students
enrichment.summary: Soccer Without Borders would run a 10-week Saturday sports program with organized recreation for newcomer elementary school students. High school-aged newcomer students would work as referees and assistant coaches to build leadership and job skills. The agreement runs from January 11 to May 25, 2024.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Soccer Without Borders - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Pays Oakland Public Education Fund up to $49,500 for school garden and food programs
enrichment.summary: Oakland Public Education Fund would support environment, food and garden programs at school sites. It would give stipends to the people who lead and care for learning spaces and run programs for students and families. The agreement runs from December 7, 2023 to June 30, 2024.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Adds $5,544 for Oakland Public Education Fund to run after-school media arts classes
enrichment.summary: This amendment adds more scope and money to an existing agreement. Oakland Public Education Fund would also teach after-school media arts classes at up to 7 elementary, middle and high school campuses, two days per campus, for up to 20 students per class. The agreement's maximum rises from $109,050 to $114,594, and the time period stays July 26, 2023 to May 23, 2024.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Amendment No. 1, Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Oakland Public Education Fund - Community Schools and Student Services Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts free remote reading tutoring from OpenLiteracy for up to 200 students at six schools
enrichment.summary: OpenLiteracy would provide remote one-on-one tutoring as an intensive extra-support program for up to 200 students, prioritizing grades 1-3. The six schools are Think College Now, Cleveland Elementary, Emerson Elementary, Oakland Academy of Knowledge, Allendale Elementary and Fruitvale Elementary. The agreement runs from January 1 to May 31, 2024 at no cost to the district.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: No-Cost Service Agreement - OpenLiteracy - Tutoring - Academics and Instruction Department

enrichment.headline: Awards Purple Communications up to $276,000 for translation and interpretation services through 2026
enrichment.summary: Purple Communications won a competitive bid (a request for proposals) to provide in-person, video, phone and document translation and interpretation to the district as needed. The agreement is capped at $276,000 for August 7, 2023 through June 30, 2026, which began before this vote. A separate data-sharing agreement covers how student information is shared with and protected by the company.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement (Award of RFP No. 22-139OE Translation and Interpretation Services) and Data Sharing Agreement – Purple Communications, Inc. - Office of Equity

enrichment.headline: Accepts a federal human trafficking prevention education grant, running through September 2028
enrichment.summary: The district would enter a cooperative agreement with the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services' Office on Trafficking in Persons to run a Human Trafficking Youth Prevention Education demonstration program. It starts September 30, 2023 and runs through September 29, 2028, with each year's continuation depending on performance, rules compliance and available funds. The text does not state a dollar amount.

items.fundingSource: United States Department of Health and Human Services

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

enrichment.headline: Ratifies up to $58,000 for Space80seven's music-industry internship for 10 Fremont High students
enrichment.summary: Space80seven would run a music-industry work-based learning internship for 10 students in Fremont High School's Media Academy. Students get personalized training plans, mentorship from industry professionals, and career field trips including a two-day trip to Los Angeles. This is a ratification, meaning the board is approving an agreement whose December 1, 2023 start came before the vote. It runs through June 30, 2024.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Space80seven, LLC - Fremont High School

enrichment.headline: Pays Bay Area Community Resources up to $3,921.50 for behavior support at Brookfield Elementary
enrichment.summary: Bay Area Community Resources would give daily support to Brookfield Elementary students with severe behavior and social-emotional challenges. Staff would meet with students one-on-one to solve problems and help supervise recess and lunch, including rainy-day schedules. The agreement period, August 21 to November 17, 2023, ended before this vote.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: Services Agreement 2023-2024 - Bay Area Community Resources - Brookfield Elementary School

enrichment.headline: Approves up to $37,855,000 for nonpublic special education schools and agencies in 2023-24
enrichment.summary: This resolution approves new master agreements and individual service agreements with nonpublic, nonsectarian schools and agencies that serve students in special education, for the 2023-2024 school year. The combined cap is $37,855,000, made up of $9,100,000 for nonpublic schools and $28,755,000 for nonpublic agencies. The individual providers are listed in attachments to the resolution.

outcome.action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

items.title: New Master Agreements or Contracts and Individual Service Agreements with Nonpublic, Nonsectarian School/Agency Services - Students of Special Education Program - School Year 2023-2024 – Special Education Department

enrichment.headline: Accepts free reading tutoring from Hoot Reading for students at six schools
enrichment.summary: Hoot Reading would run a pilot of one-on-one, high-dosage reading tutoring for 192 students at 6 schools, with virtual tutoring for 32 students at each school. Students get three 30-minute lessons a week, and a liaison helps the schools. The agreement runs January 16 to June 30, 2024 at no cost to the district, with a separate data-sharing agreement covering student information.

outcome.action: Adopted

enrichment.summary: The board is approving out-of-state student travel for 15 Elmhurst United Middle School students (grades 6-8) and 6 adults to attend the JAMZ School Cheer Nationals 2024 cheerleading competition in Las Vegas, Nevada. The trip is January 25 to 28, 2024, at no cost to the district.

enrichment.summary: The board is approving the written record of its December 14, 2023 special meeting. Staff prepared the minutes shortly after the meeting. There is no money involved.
